guide.summary: Restricted Mode, up to 25 users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public app for any YNAB user (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Restricted Mode, up to 25 users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public app for any YNAB user (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for YNAB, fine for prototypes. For production, create an auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio has a managed YNAB app. For production you should use your own app so users see your brand and get dedicated quota, and so you can request YNAB's review.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users; your own app gets dedicated quota
Restricted Mode removal is requested for your own OAuth app
Managed app default scopes may not fit your needs

prerequisites.title: YNAB account
prerequisites.detail: OAuth apps are created from Developer Settings while signed in. The account must have a confirmed email and active subscription or trial for API requests to work.

prerequisites.title: Published privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: It must explain how API data is handled, stored, secured and retained, have a Last Updated date, and offer a way to delete data. Its URL must be set in the OAuth client config.

prerequisites.title: Non-affiliation footer and compliant naming
prerequisites.detail: Add the non-affiliation language to your site footer. Names and DNS names may include YNAB only after 'for'.

steps.title: Create OAuth app in Developer Settings
steps.detail: Sign in to YNAB, open Account Settings, then Developer Settings, and click New Application. Copy the Client ID and Secret shown after saving.
steps.done_when: You have a Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the YNAB auth config via Composio's API with your own client ID and secret. Check the redirect URI matches the one set in YNAB exactly.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection completes.

steps.title: Choose read-only or full scope
steps.detail: Use the read-only scope if the agent does not need to write to a plan. Request only the minimum permissions needed.
steps.done_when: Scope choice is documented and set.

steps.title: Write and publish privacy policy
steps.detail: Draft with required elements, publish it, show it in your app, and add its URL to the OAuth client configuration. An agent can draft the text.
steps.done_when: Policy is live and linked in OAuth config.

steps.title: Submit Restricted Mode review request
steps.detail: Submit the review form for your OAuth app once it follows the API Terms and OAuth Application Requirements.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: The process takes 2-4 weeks. YNAB emails confirmation when Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: The API allows up to 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: The API allows up to 200 requests per hour, with the limit resetting every clock hour (page does not say this limit differs for unreviewed apps).

traps.title: 25-user cap blocks new sign-ups
traps.detail: Once 25 non-owner tokens are issued, the Authorization screen shows a message and new authorizations are prohibited. Request review before reaching it, as the wait is 2-4 weeks.

traps.title: Access tokens expire after 2 hours
traps.detail: Use the Authorization Code Grant so refresh tokens work. The Implicit Grant has no refresh tokens and users must re-authorize.

traps.title: Each token is limited to 200 requests per hour
traps.detail: Plan agent call volume per user token accordingly.

traps.title: App can be disabled for policy breaches
traps.detail: Breaking the API Terms or OAuth Application Requirements disables the application, and YNAB may suspend access at any time without notice.

traps.title: Composio callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: YNAB requires the redirect URI to match the one configured exactly. If you want to hide Composio's domain, proxy the callback through your own domain with a 302 redirect and register that URI in YNAB.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen says the limit is reached and new authorizations are prohibited
blockers.what_it_means: The app is still in Restricted Mode and has issued 25 non-owner tokens.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit the review form and wait 2-4 weeks.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the app against the OAuth Application Requirements before submission.

blockers.symptom: 403 subscription_lapsed, trial_expired or email_unconfirmed on API calls
blockers.what_it_means: The YNAB account being used has a lapsed subscription, expired trial or unconfirmed email.
blockers.what_to_do: Have the user fix their account status.

open_questions: Whether the 2-4 week review has stricter checks beyond policy adherence: ask YNAB API support or read the OAuth Application Requirements.
Whether the 200 requests per hour limit differs after review: ask YNAB API support.
Whether YNAB charges for API access: not found in the dossier.

evidence.answer: To create an OAuth application, you sign in to your YNAB account, go to Account Settings, then Developer Settings.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: In 2023 it moved to https://api.ynab.com/v1 .
evidence.answer: The API moved in 2023 from the older youneedabudget.com base URL to https://api.ynab.com/v1, which is the URL all consumers should use.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: The email address for this account has not been confirmed.
evidence.answer: API requests from an account whose email address is not confirmed are refused with a 403 email_unconfirmed error.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is created, it will be placed in Restricted Mode initially.
evidence.answer: A newly created OAuth application starts in Restricted Mode.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: This means the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: In Restricted Mode, the application can obtain access tokens for only 25 users other than the application owner.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: To have Restricted Mode removed, you must request a review via this form .
evidence.answer: To remove Restricted Mode, the developer must submit a review request through a form on the page.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once we review the application and confirm adherence to our policies, we will remove Restricted Mode and send you an email confirmation.
evidence.answer: YNAB reviews the application against its policies before removing Restricted Mode and then emails the developer a confirmation.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You can use it to build a personal application to interact with your own plan or build an application that any other YNABer can authorize and use.
evidence.answer: The API can be used to build an application that any other YNAB user can authorize and use.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: OAuth is the only option for obtaining access tokens for other users .
evidence.answer: OAuth is the only way to get access tokens for other users.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You must publish a privacy policy that is displayed to users.
evidence.answer: The developer must publish a privacy policy that is displayed to users.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: YNAB is not responsible for reviewing your Privacy Policy and determining whether it is compliant with all applicable privacy laws.
evidence.answer: YNAB states that it does not review the developer's privacy policy for compliance with privacy laws.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A clear explanation of how the data obtained through the YNAB API will be handled, stored, secured, and how long it will be kept, which must be accurate and comprehensive.
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must explain how YNAB API data is handled, stored, secured, and how long it is kept.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A "Last Updated" date
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must include a Last Updated date.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: A method for users to delete their data if they request it (can be a contact email).
evidence.answer: The privacy policy must give users a method to delete their data on request, which can be a contact email.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available and ensure that it is prominently displayed in your application interface so that users can find this information easily.
evidence.answer: When the application is publicly available, the privacy policy URL must be set in the OAuth client configuration and shown prominently in the app.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: When an OAuth application is requesting authorization, a scope parameter with a value of read-only can be passed to request read-only access to a plan.
evidence.answer: An OAuth authorization request can include a scope value of read-only to request read-only access to a plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If an access token issued with the read-only scope is used when requesting an endpoint that modifies the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.) a 403 Forbidden response will be issued.
evidence.answer: A read-only token used on an endpoint that modifies the plan receives a 403 Forbidden response.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If you do not need write access to a plan, please use the read-only scope.
evidence.answer: The developer should use the read-only scope if write access to a plan is not needed.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Only request the minimum necessary permissions to run your application, features, or services and don’t request access to information that you don’t need.
evidence.answer: Developers must request only the minimum permissions their application needs, and should request access in context via incremental authorization where possible.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Request access in context, via incremental authorization, wherever possible.
evidence.answer: Developers should request access in context, via incremental authorization, wherever possible.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This means the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: Restricted Mode limits an unreviewed OAuth application to 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Once this limit is reached, a message will be placed on the Authorization screen and new authorizations will be prohibited.
evidence.answer: Once the 25-token limit is reached, the Authorization screen shows a message and new authorizations are prohibited.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour .
evidence.answer: Any access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour, enforced within a rolling one-hour window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type does not support refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the user must be prompted again to authorize your application.
evidence.answer: Under the Implicit Grant, access tokens expire 2 hours after being granted, there are no refresh tokens, and the user must authorize again.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type supports refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the application can request a new access token without having to prompt the user to authorize again.
evidence.answer: Under the Authorization Code Grant, access tokens expire 2 hours after being granted, but refresh tokens let the app get a new token without prompting the user again.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This new token will not expire but can be revoked at any time from this same screen.
evidence.answer: A Personal Access Token does not expire but can be revoked at any time.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: The Restricted Mode removal review takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: Requests from an account whose subscription has lapsed are refused with a 403 subscription_lapsed error.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: Requests from an account whose trial has expired are refused with a 403 trial_expired error.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: The API may only be used when a YNAB account owner has explicitly given permission through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access:
evidence.answer: Each end user is shown an approval screen where they grant your application access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application:
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user is asked to choose a default plan when authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Personal Access Tokens are access tokens created by an account owner and are intended to be used only by that same account owner.
evidence.answer: Personal Access Tokens are meant only for the account owner who created them and should not be shared.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI must match the one configured when the OAuth application was set up, and it must be the same value used in the authorization request.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The client ID and redirect URI used in the authorization request are the values configured when the OAuth application was created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests to ensure communication from your client to our endpoint is encrypted, end-to-end.
evidence.answer: TLS (HTTPS) is enforced on all API requests, so communication to YNAB's endpoint is encrypted.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: After saving a new OAuth application, its Client ID and Client Secret are shown on its details page.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Here, you specify the details of your application and save it.
evidence.answer: You create the application by clicking New Application under the OAuth Applications section of Developer Settings, then specifying its details and saving.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant .
evidence.answer: The API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The Authorization Code Grant type, also informally known as the "server-side flow", is intended for server-side applications, where the application Secret can be protected .
evidence.answer: The Authorization Code Grant is intended for server-side applications where the client secret can be protected.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: client_secret - The client secret provided when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The client secret is supplied in the token request parameters, as the secret provided when the OAuth application was set up.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: An OAuth application can optionally have default plan selection enabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: All OAuth Application integrations must abide by the API Terms of Service and the OAuth Application Requirements . Failure to do so will result in disabling of the application.
evidence.answer: All OAuth integrations must follow the API Terms of Service and the OAuth Application Requirements, or the application will be disabled.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The app name and web address may not include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by the word 'for'.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any graphics or artwork may not be modifications to our official branding and must be distinguishable from YNAB itself and/or from YNAB’s graphics or artwork.
evidence.answer: Graphics and artwork must not modify YNAB's official branding and must be distinguishable from YNAB's artwork.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Developers may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Somewhere on your site page, please add the following language at the footer:
evidence.answer: Developers must add a non-affiliation disclaimer to their site footer.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You are NEVER ALLOWED to directly request, handle or store credentials associated with users’ financial accounts.
evidence.answer: Developers are never allowed to directly request, handle, or store credentials for users' financial accounts.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Access tokens must be handled securely and never be exposed to a third party.
evidence.answer: Access tokens must be handled securely and never exposed to a third party.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13. The minimum age for a user to use YNAB is 13.
evidence.answer: The application may not be directed at children under 13, and the minimum age to use YNAB is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Maintain a secure operating environment.
evidence.answer: Developers must maintain a secure operating environment.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: (2) access, aggregate, or analyze YNAB user data if the data will be sold to a third party
evidence.answer: Developers may not access, aggregate, or analyze YNAB user data if the data will be sold to a third party.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: YNAB may terminate or suspend any and all access to the API immediately at any time, without prior notice or liability at our sole discretion.
evidence.answer: YNAB sets and enforces API limits at its discretion, and may terminate or suspend API access at any time without prior notice.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: Provider-stated (not a developer report): removing Restricted Mode from a YNAB OAuth app after a review request takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: the application will be limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner.
evidence.answer: Provider-stated blocker: a new YNAB OAuth app starts in Restricted Mode and can authorize only 25 non-owner users until the review removes the limit.
